title: Five Pull Requests Change the Policy
part: The release, in the order it runs
html:
Five Pull Requests Change the Policy

Pull requestChangesSmoke scenariosEnds
501renewals: 2 weeks5 of 5promoted to Dev
502renewals: 4 weeks5 of 5promoted to Dev
503renewals: 1 week5 of 5promoted to Dev
504renewals: none (0 weeks)??
505a README line only5 of 5promoted to Dev

Merged, built, smoke-tested, promoted only if every scenario passes. Guess which one is in trouble.
say: Remember the policy file? Now it's in the library's repository, and people send pull requests that change it. Here are five, run for real. One makes renewals two weeks. One makes them four. One makes them one week. One makes them none at all: zero weeks. And one only changes a line in the README. Each pull request gets released the same way: merged, built by Jenkins, smoke-tested against what Jenkins deployed, and promoted to Dev, but only if every smoke scenario passes. One of the smoke scenarios checks that renewing a book moves its due date. You can probably guess which pull request is in trouble. Let's follow a release through, in the order it runs.
